one worked buttonhole beside that single button, as drawn

notes:
ADVERSARIAL READ vs /images/blueprints/supplier/71e4a88d0f42__0623__1_button_32L.jpg.

WHAT THE DRAWING SPECIFIES: a jacket sleeve end in profile carrying ONE red button symbol (an elongated oval with a bar through it — one button plus its buttonhole) set against the sleeve's rear edge at roughly 40% of the cuff height above the hem. Nothing else is marked.

ATTEMPTED REJECTIONS THAT FAILED:
(1) Count drift to the conventional four-button jacket cuff — the commonest failure on this field? No. There is exactly ONE button and ONE buttonhole; the cuff above it is bare cloth with no stitch marks, no shadow buttons, no second buttonhole.
(2) Geometry borrowed from a neighbouring option on the same field (cb-none, cb-2, cb-3)? No — one button, distinct from all of them.
(3) Annotation traced — did it render the drawing's red? No. The button is tonal horn on brown hopsack; there is no red, no number, no arrow and no leader line anywhere in frame.
(4) Wrong face of the garment substituted? No; this is unambiguously the sleeve end, with its vent seam and hem.
(5) Blind button sewn straight to the cloth with no buttonhole? No — a worked buttonhole is clearly visible beside the button, as drawn.
(6) Button on the wrong edge of the sleeve? No — it sits against the rear/vent edge exactly where the drawing places it.

No critical or major findings.
